questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when you see animals near the road. Animals may suddenly move or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so more may be nearby and out of sight.

questions.question: How do you check for vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Look in the inside rearview mirror.
Look in the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, how should you do it?

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely to restore your view of the road. Return to your lane only when you can see both of the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, which parts should you use?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: What does California's Move Over law require?

options.text: All vehicles must stay in the right lane at all times.
Trucks must use the left lane.
All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road, move away from that lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move safely, slow down and proceed with caution. This law also applies to stopped tow trucks and Department of Transportation vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Use high beam lights in fog.
Stare at the road directly ahead of your vehicle.
Check your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: To stay aware, check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds and scan the road. Staring straight ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. Making a left turn here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and continuously pass cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and safer.
You will increase your chances of a collision.
You will help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Every time you pass a vehicle, your collision risk increases.

questions.question: How far ahead of your vehicle should you look to avoid last-minute moves?

options.text: 5 to 10 seconds.
10 to 15 seconds.
15 to 20 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to see hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start to occur on wet roads?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot channel water well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and ride over water like water skis.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a curved ramp going downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is not working, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, then proceed when safe.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as if stop signs control it from all directions. Stop and only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the benefit of keeping a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Other drivers can cut in front, which improves traffic flow.
You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It inflates to protect you in a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to safely react to another driver's mistake. Extra space may let you brake or move out of the way of a vehicle entering your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black lettering means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads at the start of areas where you cannot pass.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive slower in bad weather to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: You want to pass a cyclist in a narrow lane. An oncoming car is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and then pass the cyclist.
Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first.
Wait until the cyclist leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one danger at a time. Let the oncoming car pass you first. Then pass the cyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: You are making a right turn. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn right away.
Stop before the right lane and let all traffic go first.
Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Slow down, stop at the line if needed, then make your turn.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish its turn first.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish its turn first.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: A child on a bicycle is near your vehicle. What should you expect?

options.text: The child will beep a horn.
The child has full control of the bike.
The child may do something unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The child may do something unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bikes are unpredictable. Young riders often change direction suddenly. Children and bikes are small and hard to see.

questions.question: Which of these is both dangerous AND illegal while driving?

options.text: Listening to music through both ears with headphones.
Adjusting your side mirrors.
Reading a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening to music through both ears with headphones.
questions.explanation: Wearing headphones in both ears while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the car ahead is turning left.
When there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive onto the shoulder or off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so your car rolls away from the road center if your brakes fail.

questions.question: California's Basic Speed Law says you must:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
Always drive at the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: You may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions. For example, driving 45 mph in a 55 mph zone during heavy fog is too fast for conditions, even though you are below the limit.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles driving straight. You can only turn when it is safe and does not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which roadways freeze first when wet?

options.text: Bridges and overpasses
Intersections
Tunnels

questions.correctAnswerText: Bridges and overpasses
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.question: To turn left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start from:

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.
Any lane, as long as it seems safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Start left turns from the far left lane. Watch for pedestrians, motorcyclists, and cyclists between you and the curb. They can also use the left turn lane. Turn into any open lane that is safe.

questions.question: You hit an animal with your car on a California highway. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured animal off the road.
Call the humane society.
Keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call the humane society.
questions.explanation: Call the police, CHP, or the nearest humane society. Do not move the animal or leave it to suffer.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in a residential area is:

options.text: 20 mph.
25 mph.
30 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in residential and business areas is 25 mph.

questions.question: What usually causes a locked wheel skid?

options.text: Braking too hard at a slow speed
Braking lightly at a slow speed
Braking too hard at a high speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking too hard at a high speed
questions.explanation: Locked wheel skids usually happen when a driver brakes too hard while going fast. Use your brakes smoothly and gradually.
